scope: Seven external orchestration systems (Temporal, Argo Workflows, Apache Airflow, Prefect/Dagster, Restate, Windmill, Ray) surveyed for features that are genuinely adoptable by mini-ork, with each candidate marked against an existing partial surface in the engine or called out as a gap. The space-surveyor pass for the 20261012-langgraph-parity-survey family; siblings cover lens-D1 (langgraph auditor), lens-D3 (persistence / checkpointers), and lens-D4 (streaming modes).
citation_convention: Every feature's claim line carries at least one inline citation — either a relative file:line anchor that resolves in the worktree or the literal 'GAP' for missing surfaces. The citation sits in the `citations` array of each claim (D1 hard rule C4), so a grep on the claim returns a citation.
yaml_convention: Every feature ends with an `Adopt?` verdict from the closed enum {partial, extend, adopt, skip} (D1 hard rule F4). The verdict is preserved verbatim in each claim's `miniork_status`.

claims.feature: Temporal — durable event history with deterministic replay
claims.semantics_summary: The foundation that makes every other Temporal feature possible: workflows are deterministic replayers driven by an event history. The run_events table written by mini_ork/observability/node_events.py:235 already records node lifecycle rows on the same insert path; mini-ork just does not replay from them — classify_outcome at mini_ork/orchestration/runner_orchestrator.py:216 decides the terminal finish reason off the last row, not the whole history.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Closes the durable-execution parity axis — without replay, no continue-as-new, no journaled resume, no signal/update queries worth their name; this single feature gates most of §1's downstream work.
claims.value_any_task: Any long-running recipe that crashes mid-run benefits; the journal becomes the foundation for every recovery story the chapter might tell.
claims.proposed_shape: Extend run_events into a replay source: have classify_outcome read the whole history (not just the last row) and add a replayer path that resumes from a chosen checkpoint row.

claims.feature: Temporal — workflow versioning with PATCHED / getVersion()
claims.semantics_summary: Lets a non-backwards-compatible code change ship without forking in-progress runs. CompiledRetryEdge at mini_ork/recovery/dag.py:41 carries a version field that is consulted when reloading a workflow after recovery, but the consumer side at mini_ork/recovery/dag.py:175 (load_dag) ignores it on re-load.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Tightens the load path to refuse mismatched versions; small, scoped, and unblocks recipe-version-bump shipping.
claims.value_any_task: Every recipe benefits — author migrations become a one-line verification instead of a manual reconciliation.
claims.proposed_shape: Make load_dag at mini_ork/recovery/dag.py:175 honor the version on CompiledRetryEdge and refuse reload on mismatch.

claims.feature: Temporal — signals, queries, and the update RPC
claims.semantics_summary: External mid-flight intervention without forking the run. The steering guard at mini_ork/orchestration/runner_orchestrator.py:321 (guard_steer) and renderer at mini_ork/orchestration/runner_orchestrator.py:334 (steer_message) are exactly this in miniature, fed by steer_run at mini_ork/web/control.py:550. The surface is the same shape as Temporal updates; the gap is that mini-ork's guard rejects messages that touch routing/termination (guard_steer only returns True for HELP-class messages), so the expressiveness is narrower than Temporal's full update protocol.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Keep the guard semantics; expose a typed-payload variant for richer queries — the steering channel is already mini-ork's update protocol in spirit.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that need mid-flight parameter changes use steer_run today; a typed payload widens the addressable use cases without relaxing the guard.
claims.proposed_shape: Add a typed-payload variant to steer_message; document guard_steer as the canonical safety filter.

claims.feature: Temporal — schedules (cron + skip + backfill)
claims.semantics_summary: Cron-like scheduled recipe invocation with skip/backfill semantics. The scheduler module under mini_ork/scheduler.py exists but is outside the orchestration core — there is no bridge from a schedule hit to a recipe kickoff yet.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Real cron-like schedules are the largest piece of the operational tooling the chapter currently lacks.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that want nightly or hourly execution need it; today, recipes are kickoff-driven or ad-hoc CLI.
claims.proposed_shape: Wire mini_ork/scheduler.py into the engine entry as a schedule-to-kickoff bridge.

claims.feature: Temporal — continue-as-new bound
claims.semantics_summary: Caps history growth on long-running workflows by checkpointing and starting a fresh history. _post_run_learning at mini_ork/cli/execute.py:1473 performs a write-back at run close that is analogous (a checkpoint-style summary), but mini-ork has no in-run continue-as-new analogue.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Long-running recipes need a bound on history growth; this is contingent on the durable-replay story landing first.
claims.value_any_task: Any recipe whose run_events table would grow past practical limits benefits.
claims.proposed_shape: Add an in-run continue-as-new analogue: when run_events grows past a threshold, summarize and start a fresh history row.

claims.feature: Argo Workflows — templated, reusable step definitions
claims.semantics_summary: Lets the same step shape serve many recipes without copy-paste. The DAG model at mini_ork/recovery/dag.py:130 has edges and node IDs but no template indirection — every consumer embeds the concrete node.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Template indirection closes a long-standing recipe-authoring pain point: shared step shapes without copy-paste.
claims.value_any_task: Any recipe family with shared sub-shapes (e.g. verifier tiers, learning writeback) benefits.
claims.proposed_shape: Add a template indirection layer to DAG at mini_ork/recovery/dag.py:130 — node IDs that resolve to a named template at compile time.

claims.feature: Argo Workflows — artifact passing between steps with S3-compatible storage
claims.semantics_summary: Large outputs cannot flow through the run_events table. mini_ork/cache.py:145 (emit) already records per-stage artifacts keyed by input_hash, but there is no first-class artifact bus between sibling nodes; consumers reach into the run directory.
claims.value_chapter_epic: A first-class artifact bus between sibling nodes closes the gap where consumers reach into the run directory.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that pass large outputs between sibling stages use the new bus instead of filesystem-level sharing.
claims.proposed_shape: Promote the input_hash-keyed emit at mini_ork/cache.py:145 into a sibling-node artifact bus surface.

claims.feature: Argo Workflows — retry with backoff and exit-hook handlers
claims.semantics_summary: The difference between transient retry and definitive failure is the first thing an on-call asks for. CompiledRetryEdge at mini_ork/recovery/dag.py:41 carries retry metadata that _apply_recovery_filter at mini_ork/cli/execute.py:649 honors, but there is no exit-handler node — on permanent failure the run just terminates and the recipe's reflect step learns about it.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Add an exit-handler node that fires on permanent failure; keeps the existing retry surface intact.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that need a cleanup path on terminal failure use the exit handler.
claims.proposed_shape: Add a node type 'exit_handler' to the WorkflowNode enum; the executor routes to it on permanent failure.

claims.feature: Argo Workflows — suspend / resume with TTL
claims.semantics_summary: Long human-in-the-loop approvals should not hold a worker open. pause_cost_run at mini_ork/web/control.py:46 and resume_cost_run at mini_ork/web/control.py:86 are exactly this for cost-only pauses; the gap is that there is no DAG-level suspend for non-cost waits.
claims.value_chapter_epic: DAG-level suspend with TTL closes the gap where cost-pause is the only pause primitive.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that wait on human approvals or external systems benefit.
claims.proposed_shape: Generalize pause_cost_run at mini_ork/web/control.py:46 into a DAG-level suspend with TTL.

claims.feature: Argo Workflows — workflow-of-workflows (sub-workflows)
claims.semantics_summary: One run spawning another with explicit parent-child linkage. mo_recursive_approve_spawn at mini_ork/orchestration/recursive.py:171 already inserts a run_spawns row linking parent to child with an authority_level gate (see default_authority_level at mini_ork/orchestration/recursive.py:116). This is more conservative than Argo's sub-workflow model because of the authority check, but it is the same shape.
claims.value_chapter_epic: The authority gate is a deliberate hardening over Argo's sub-workflow model; preserve it and document why.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that need parent-child composition use mo_recursive_approve_spawn today.
claims.proposed_shape: Document the authority-gated sub-workflow model as the canonical composition pattern.

claims.feature: Argo Workflows — parameterization at submit time
claims.semantics_summary: Lets the same workflow take different inputs without forking definitions. The ExecuteArgs dataclass at mini_ork/cli/execute.py:548 already parses most knobs from argv, and _parse_execute_argv at mini_ork/cli/execute.py:560 threads them through. The gap is that there is no recipe-level parameter schema — knobs are positional strings.
claims.value_chapter_epic: A typed recipe-level parameter schema closes the gap where knobs are positional strings.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that take runtime parameters declare them on a parameter block.
claims.proposed_shape: Add a `parameters:` block to workflow.yaml (or task_class.yaml) with a jsonschema-typed schema.

claims.feature: Apache Airflow — XCom-style small-payload inter-task data
claims.semantics_summary: Tiny values (decisions, IDs, short summaries) should not require an artifact round-trip. The run_events table records (key, value)-style payloads — see mo_node_emit at mini_ork/observability/node_events.py:165 — but there is no queryable XCom view; consumers have to scrape run_events rows.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Surface a queryable XCom view on top of run_events instead of having consumers scrape rows.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that pass small values between stages use the XCom view.
claims.proposed_shape: Add an XCom view query helper on top of run_events at mini_ork/observability/node_events.py:165.

claims.feature: Apache Airflow — scheduler with backfills and catchup
claims.semantics_summary: mini-ork has no scheduler at all today — runs are CLI- or kickoff-driven. mini_ork/scheduler.py exists as a module but is not wired into the engine entry; _resolve_dispatch_mode at mini_ork/cli/execute.py:317 selects serial / parallel / etc. but not a schedule this DAG at cron mode.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Real scheduling is the single largest operational-tooling gap; without it, Temporal's schedule feature and Airflow's scheduler feature are both blocked.
claims.value_any_task: Every recipe that wants time-based invocation benefits; today there is no cron path.
claims.proposed_shape: Wire mini_ork/scheduler.py into the engine entry; add a 'scheduled' dispatch mode to _resolve_dispatch_mode at mini_ork/cli/execute.py:317.

claims.feature: Apache Airflow — connections and variables as first-class config
claims.semantics_summary: Secrets and per-environment overrides should not be YAML literals in recipes. mini_ork/context.py:94 resolves MINI_ORK_DB and home paths, and mini_ork/cli/execute.py reads MINI_ORK_* env vars — the env contract already exists. The gap is the secret-store side: secrets come from the process env, not a vault.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Adopt the vault surface via the two-tier pattern (env now, vault later) — see config/vault.example.yaml.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that need per-environment secrets use the vault tier; the env tier keeps the simple-tier shape.
claims.proposed_shape: Land the vault tier described in config/vault.example.yaml; document the two-tier fallback (env → vault).

claims.feature: Apache Airflow — pools and SLAs
claims.semantics_summary: Bound concurrency per resource; bound total wall-clock per task. _max_parallel at mini_ork/cli/execute.py:398 is mini-ork's whole concurrency story — global, not per-pool. SLAs do not exist.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Per-pool concurrency and SLAs are both missing; one task adds both.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes with per-resource concurrency ceilings (e.g., GPU, rate-limited APIs) use pools.
claims.proposed_shape: Replace _max_parallel at mini_ork/cli/execute.py:398 with a named-pool map and add a per-task SLA field.

claims.feature: Apache Airflow — task instances with retry + try_number
claims.semantics_summary: The operator needs to know this is attempt 3 of 7 without reading logs. record_hit at mini_ork/cache.py:129 records cache hits keyed by (epic_id, stage, input_hash) — the cache hit count is structurally similar to try_number but is not surfaced to the operator.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Surface cache hits as attempt counts in the run summary — one-line addition.
claims.value_any_task: Every recipe that retries benefits from operator-visible attempt counts.
claims.proposed_shape: Surface record_hit's cache hit count at mini_ork/cache.py:129 in the run_summary.

claims.feature: Apache Airflow — DAG-level start_date / end_date filters
claims.semantics_summary: Lets old DAGs stop accepting new runs. _post_run_learning at mini_ork/cli/execute.py:1473 runs once at close but there is no pre-flight guard against running an expired recipe.
claims.value_chapter_epic: A pre-flight guard against running an expired recipe closes the operational gap.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes with a sunset date use the guard to refuse new runs.
claims.proposed_shape: Add an expires_on field to workflow.yaml and a pre-flight check that refuses runs after the expiry.

claims.feature: Prefect/Dagster — asset-keyed runs
claims.semantics_summary: The operator thinks in this dashboard is stale, not the 02:00 DAG missed. cache.lookup at mini_ork/cache.py:107 keys by (epic_id, stage, input_hash) — the epic_id is the closest thing to an asset key in mini-ork today, but it is opaque to the UI; _classification_dag at mini_ork/ide_pages/dags.py:97 does not project it as a graph node.
claims.value_chapter_epic: The largest structural parity gap — asset-keyed runs would unlock sensors, asset catalog, and lineage views at once.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that produce a tracked output (dashboard, model artifact) get asset-keyed freshness tracking.
claims.proposed_shape: Promote epic_id to a first-class asset key; project it as a node in _classification_dag at mini_ork/ide_pages/dags.py:97.

claims.feature: Prefect/Dagster — sensors / triggers that wait on an upstream state
claims.semantics_summary: Lets a run start only when its source data is ready, instead of polling. The steering channel (steer_run at mini_ork/web/control.py:550, guard at mini_ork/orchestration/runner_orchestrator.py:321) can nudge a running node; the gap is that there is no wait-for-state primitive — the run has to keep retrying.
claims.value_chapter_epic: A wait-for-state primitive closes the polling workaround.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that depend on upstream freshness wait cleanly instead of polling.
claims.proposed_shape: Add a 'wait_for_state' node type that blocks until a named asset state matches.

claims.feature: Prefect/Dagster — materialized asset catalog
claims.semantics_summary: In Dagster, every run leaves a row in the asset catalog with a partition key. run_summary at mini_ork/cache.py:184 produces a job-level summary string; there is no per-asset catalog table.
claims.value_chapter_epic: A per-asset catalog table is the durable surface behind asset-keyed runs.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that produce tracked assets record catalog rows.
claims.proposed_shape: Add a per-asset catalog table that run_summary at mini_ork/cache.py:184 writes into.

claims.feature: Prefect/Dagster — flow-level retries with stateful checkpoints
claims.semantics_summary: Retries should resume from the last successful sub-step, not re-run the whole flow. mini_ork/cache.py:145 (emit) and lookup at mini_ork/cache.py:107 together give a per-stage cache that does this for cacheable stages; non-cacheable stages are still all-or-nothing.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Extend the per-stage cache to non-cacheable stages so the resume story covers everything.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes with mixed cacheable / non-cacheable stages benefit; retries resume mid-flow instead of restarting.
claims.proposed_shape: Generalize the cache.emit / lookup pair at mini_ork/cache.py:107 to cover non-cacheable stages.

claims.feature: Prefect/Dagster — dynamic fan-out at runtime
claims.semantics_summary: The number of subtasks is only known after the first task runs. _run_parallel_batch at mini_ork/cli/execute.py:489 and the mirror at mini_ork/orchestration/runner_orchestrator.py:489 already parallelize a fixed list; the gap is that the list is computed before the batch starts, not during it.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Dynamic fan-out closes the gap where the task list is fixed at batch start.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes whose subtask count depends on first-task results use the dynamic shape.
claims.proposed_shape: Allow _run_parallel_batch at mini_ork/cli/execute.py:489 to accept a generator-shaped input list.

claims.feature: Prefect/Dagster — versioned asset lineage
claims.semantics_summary: Know which run produced the row in the dashboard today. run_artifact_edges (see the module docstring at mini_ork/orchestration/recursive.py:18) is inserted by mo_recursive_record_artifact at mini_ork/orchestration/recursive.py:389, but the lineage view is not exposed in mini_ork/ide_pages/dags.py — _classification_dag at mini_ork/ide_pages/dags.py:97 shows the classification graph, not the artifact graph.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Expose the lineage view in the IDE pages — close the gap where the artifact graph is internal-only.
claims.value_any_task: Every recipe that produces artifacts benefits from the visible lineage view.
claims.proposed_shape: Add a lineage view alongside _classification_dag at mini_ork/ide_pages/dags.py:97.

claims.feature: Restate — durable queue with exactly-once semantics
claims.semantics_summary: Lets external callers enqueue work without coordinating with the engine. dispatch_mode (see _resolve_dispatch_mode at mini_ork/cli/execute.py:317) selects serial / parallel for internal parallelism; there is no inbound queue surface at all.
claims.value_chapter_epic: An inbound queue surface is the largest missing entry point for external callers.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that need external enqueue get a queue surface instead of CLI-only invocation.
claims.proposed_shape: Add an inbound queue surface alongside _resolve_dispatch_mode at mini_ork/cli/execute.py:317.

claims.feature: Restate — idempotency keys with replay-safe handlers
claims.semantics_summary: If a caller retries an enqueue, the handler runs once. The input_hash cache keyed by (epic_id, stage, input_hash) at mini_ork/cache.py:107 is structurally an idempotency-key cache for the internal dispatch path; there is no inbound idempotency contract.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Generalize input_hash into an idempotency key the UI surfaces — small step, real value.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that need replay-safe handler semantics get them via the existing input_hash path.
claims.proposed_shape: Surface the input_hash cache key at mini_ork/cache.py:107 as an idempotency key in the run summary.

claims.feature: Restate — journaled execution with deterministic replay
claims.semantics_summary: Restart from the journal after a crash. run_events written by mini_ork/observability/node_events.py:235 is the journal; the engine does not currently read it on resume — _apply_recovery_filter at mini_ork/cli/execute.py:649 is the only resume path and it filters nodes, not events.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Read run_events on resume instead of just filtering nodes — the journal is the source of truth.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that crash mid-run benefit from journal-driven resume instead of node-filter-driven recovery.
claims.proposed_shape: Make _apply_recovery_filter at mini_ork/cli/execute.py:649 consult the run_events journal on resume.

claims.feature: Restate — awakeables (callbacks that wake a suspended workflow)
claims.semantics_summary: A workflow can pause waiting for an external system that will call back later. The steering channel (steer_run at mini_ork/web/control.py:550) is exactly this for the operator — the gap is that no automated system can produce a wake-up.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Let automated systems produce wake-ups on the steering channel — same shape, wider source.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that wait on external callbacks get automated wake-ups instead of operator-only.
claims.proposed_shape: Allow steer_run at mini_ork/web/control.py:550 to accept a programmatic payload from any caller.

claims.feature: Restate — saga / compensating handlers
claims.semantics_summary: Workflows that fan out to many side effects need a way to roll back on partial failure. merge_decisions at mini_ork/orchestration/recursive.py:436 and the run_spawns lifecycle (mo_recursive_approve_spawn at mini_ork/orchestration/recursive.py:171) cover a forward merge; there is no saga-rollback path.
claims.value_chapter_epic: A saga-rollback path complements the forward merge — needed for any fan-out to side effects.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that fan out to many side effects roll back on partial failure.
claims.proposed_shape: Add a saga-rollback node type that walks back a forward merge_decisions sequence at mini_ork/orchestration/recursive.py:436.

claims.feature: Windmill — versioned scripts with explicit input/output schemas
claims.semantics_summary: The UI can render a form from the schema, and the engine can validate at submit. ExecuteArgs at mini_ork/cli/execute.py:548 and the _parse_execute_argv path at mini_ork/cli/execute.py:560 give typed argv parsing, but the schema is hand-rolled and not surfaced to mini_ork/ide_pages/.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Surface the argv schema to the UI for non-engineer triggering.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that want a UI form for triggering benefit from surfaced schemas.
claims.proposed_shape: Surface ExecuteArgs at mini_ork/cli/execute.py:548 to mini_ork/ide_pages/ for form rendering.

claims.feature: Windmill — flows-as-code with auto-generated UI
claims.semantics_summary: Lets a non-engineer trigger the same flow the engineer wrote. The mini_ork/ide_pages/ builder pattern (see build(home, tab, args) at mini_ork/ide_pages/dags.py:132) gives an HTML view of existing runs; there is no authoring surface in mini_ork/ide_pages/ — the entry point is still the kickoff file.
claims.value_chapter_epic: An authoring surface in mini_ork/ide_pages/ closes the gap where the kickoff file is the only entry point.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that want a UI authoring path get one instead of YAML-only.
claims.proposed_shape: Extend the mini_ork/ide_pages/ builder at mini_ork/ide_pages/dags.py:132 with an authoring surface for kickoff files.

claims.feature: Windmill — per-step result cache keyed by script version + inputs
claims.semantics_summary: A re-run with the same script+inputs returns the prior result. lookup at mini_ork/cache.py:107 is exactly this for input_hash, but the cache key does not include the script version.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Extend the cache key with script version so a version bump invalidates the cache.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that iterate on the script benefit from version-aware cache invalidation.
claims.proposed_shape: Add script_version to the lookup key at mini_ork/cache.py:107.

claims.feature: Windmill — concurrent step runs with global concurrency limits
claims.semantics_summary: Stop accidentally running 200 scrapers in parallel. _max_parallel at mini_ork/cli/execute.py:398 is the whole concurrency story — one global limit, no per-script limit.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Per-script concurrency limits complement the global cap.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that hit rate-limited APIs use per-script caps.
claims.proposed_shape: Replace the single _max_parallel at mini_ork/cli/execute.py:398 with a per-script map keyed on script name.

claims.feature: Windmill — suspend/resume with resume tokens
claims.semantics_summary: A long approval should resume from where it paused, not replay the whole flow. pause_cost_run at mini_ork/web/control.py:46 and the mirror resume_cost_run at mini_ork/web/control.py:86 exist for cost pauses; there is no flow-level suspend with a checkpoint.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Flow-level suspend with a checkpoint token closes the gap where only cost pauses are supported.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that pause for long approvals use the flow-level suspend.
claims.proposed_shape: Generalize pause_cost_run at mini_ork/web/control.py:46 into flow-level suspend that emits a resume token.

claims.feature: Windmill — workspace + folder scoping
claims.semantics_summary: A Windmill workspace isolates scripts, schedules, and variables per team. The workspaces module (mini_ork/workspaces.py — see the entries at mini_ork/__init__.py) exists but is not consumed by the recipe runner.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Wire mini_ork/workspaces.py into the recipe runner so per-team isolation is real.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that want per-team scoping use the workspace module.
claims.proposed_shape: Consume mini_ork/workspaces.py from the recipe runner entry.

claims.feature: Ray — distributed actor model
claims.semantics_summary: Lets a node fan out to many workers without the engine owning the cluster. The remote session path in _provision_remote_session at mini_ork/cli/execute.py:1445 and the node-agent HTTP server at mini_ork/remote/node_agent/app.py (see post_session referenced at mini_ork/remote/node_agent/images.py:406) is a hand-rolled actor surface; there is no Ray-style autoscaler on top.
claims.value_chapter_epic: The actor surface exists — the autoscaler is the missing piece. Targets Ray as execution substrate rather than re-implementing distributed execution.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that fan out to many workers use the existing actor surface; future autoscaler adoption is a documented gap.
claims.proposed_shape: Document the actor surface as the canonical distributed-execution recipe; defer the autoscaler as a future option.

claims.feature: Ray — workflow DAG driver with re-execution on failure
claims.semantics_summary: One engine call can drive many @ray.remote calls and recover from any single failure. nodes_from_workflow at mini_ork/orchestration/runner_orchestrator.py:236 reads the same workflow shape, but the recovery path (_apply_recovery_filter at mini_ork/cli/execute.py:649) only filters nodes, not re-executes them.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Extend the recovery path to re-execute failed nodes, not just filter them.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that need single-node re-execution on partial failure use the extended path.
claims.proposed_shape: Extend _apply_recovery_filter at mini_ork/cli/execute.py:649 with a re-execution branch for failed nodes.

claims.feature: Ray — pluggable resource requests (CPU/GPU/custom)
claims.semantics_summary: Let the recipe ask for 1 GPU without hard-coding. dispatch_mode selects a parallelism shape (_resolve_dispatch_mode at mini_ork/cli/execute.py:317); there is no per-node resource request.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Per-node resource requests (CPU/GPU) are the missing ingredient for cross-cutting compute parity.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that need GPU or specific CPU counts declare them on the node.
claims.proposed_shape: Add a resources: block to WorkflowNode with cpu / gpu / custom fields.

claims.feature: Ray — object store for inter-actor payloads
claims.semantics_summary: Large outputs should not move through a control plane. The input-hash cache at mini_ork/cache.py:107 references payloads by hash but does not store them — there is no object store, only references.
claims.value_chapter_epic: An object store behind the hash-cache reference surface enables a real artifact bus.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that pass large outputs use the object store instead of hash-only references.
claims.proposed_shape: Add an object store module that backs the input-hash reference at mini_ork/cache.py:107.

claims.feature: Ray — autoscaling based on backlog
claims.semantics_summary: The cluster grows when work queues up. _max_parallel at mini_ork/cli/execute.py:398 is a static cap; _run_parallel_batch at mini_ork/cli/execute.py:489 does not observe backlog.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Backlog-aware autoscaling closes the static-cap gap.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes with variable load use backlog-aware scaling.
claims.proposed_shape: Add a backlog observer to _run_parallel_batch at mini_ork/cli/execute.py:489 that grows the cap when work queues.

claims.feature: Ray — task-level metrics (counters, histograms)
claims.semantics_summary: The operator sees per-step latency, not aggregate run latency. finish_reason_for_failure at mini_ork/orchestration/runner_orchestrator.py:107 is the only per-step telemetry exposed in the runner; there are no histograms.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Counters + histograms are the missing telemetry shape the runner already emits.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that want per-step latency visibility get the new metrics.

top_10_backlog.title: Real scheduler: wire mini_ork/scheduler.py into the engine entry as a schedule-to-kickoff bridge
top_10_backlog.rationale: Airflow §3.2 + Temporal §1.5 both hinge on the same missing scheduler; the largest single operational-tooling gap in the chapter.

top_10_backlog.title: Asset-keyed runs + sensors + asset catalog: promote epic_id to a first-class asset key
top_10_backlog.rationale: Prefect/Dagster §1 + §2 + §3 form the asset-keyed parity triangle; resolving it unlocks sensors, catalog, and lineage at once.

top_10_backlog.title: Durable replay from run_events: have classify_outcome read the whole history
top_10_backlog.rationale: Temporal §1 + Restate §4 share the journaled-execution parity axis; without it no continue-as-new, no journaled resume.

top_10_backlog.title: Inbound queue surface: external enqueue for engineers without coordinate rules
top_10_backlog.rationale: Restate §1 is the cleanest queue gap; without it mini-ork has no inbound entry point for external callers.

top_10_backlog.title: Vault tier: env-now / vault-later two-tier pattern for secrets
top_10_backlog.rationale: Airflow §3 demands secrets out of YAML; the two-tier pattern preserves the simple tier while closing the secret gap.

top_10_backlog.title: Saga rollback path: complement the forward merge_decisions with a backward walker
top_10_backlog.rationale: Restate §7 closes the partial-failure rollback gap; needed for any fan-out to side effects.

top_10_backlog.title: Per-pool concurrency + SLAs: replace _max_parallel with a named-pool map and per-task SLAs
top_10_backlog.rationale: Airflow §4 closes the global-cap gap; one task adds both per-pool caps and per-task SLAs.

top_10_backlog.title: Resume-token flow-level suspend: generalize pause_cost_run to a checkpointed suspend
top_10_backlog.rationale: Argo §4 + Windmill §5 share the suspend-with-token gap; one generalization closes both.

top_10_backlog.title: Dynamic fan-out + object store: feed real subtask lists and back-do hits
top_10_backlog.rationale: Prefect/Dagster §6 + Ray §4 share the dynamic shape; the object store backs it for large outputs.

top_10_backlog.title: Telemetry + IDE lineage: surface task-level metrics + run_artifact_edges in the IDE pages
top_10_backlog.rationale: Ray §6 + Prefect/Dagster §7 share the visibility story; counters/histograms on the runner, lineage view on the IDE pages.

chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.title: Operational tooling — scheduler + per-pool concurrency + SLAs
chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.detail: mini_ork has no real scheduler, no per-pool concurrency, and no per-task SLAs. Airflow §3.2 + §3.4 and Temporal §1.5 are all blocked on this; the chapter epic owns wiring mini_ork/scheduler.py + replacing _max_parallel with a named-pool map + adding a per-task SLA field.

chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.title: Asset-keyed parity — asset-keyed runs + sensors + catalog + lineage
chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.detail: The largest structural parity gap. Prefect/Dagster §4.1 + §4.2 + §4.3 + §4.7 form a coupled decision; the chapter epic owns promoting epic_id to a first-class asset key and surfacing the lineage view in mini_ork/ide_pages/dags.py.

chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.title: Durable execution — journal-driven replay + continue-as-new
chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.detail: Temporal §1.1 + §1.6 + Restate §5.4 share the journaled-execution parity axis; the chapter epic owns reading run_events on resume and adding an in-run continue-as-new analogue.

chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.title: Inbound surfaces — queue + object store + awakeables
chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.detail: mini-ork has no inbound queue, no object store, and no automated wake-ups. Restate §5.1 + §5.5 + Ray §7.4 are coupled; the chapter epic owns shipping the queue surface + the object store behind input_hash + generalizing steer_run to programmatic payloads.

chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.title: Saga / compensating handlers — rollback path for fan-out to side effects
chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.detail: merge_decisions at mini_ork/orchestration/recursive.py:436 covers forward merge, no saga rollback. Restate §5.7 is the concrete gap; the chapter epic owns adding a saga-rollback node type.

chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.title: Secrets — vault tier with env-tier fallback
chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.detail: Secrets come from the process env today; Airflow §3.3 demands a vault tier. The chapter epic owns shipping config/vault.example.yaml with the env-tier fallback so the simple tier stays simple.

chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.title: UI authoring — flows-as-code with auto-generated UI
chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.detail: The kickoff file is the only entry point today; Windmill §6.2 demands a UI authoring surface. The chapter epic owns extending mini_ork/ide_pages/dags.py:132 with a kickoff-authoring surface.

chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.title: Resume tokens — checkpoint-token suspend that survives long approvals
chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.detail: pause_cost_run at mini_ork/web/control.py:46 is cost-only. Argo §2.4 + Windmill §6.5 share the suspend-with-token gap; the chapter epic owns generalizing to flow-level suspend with a checkpoint token.

chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.title: Citation convention C4 propagation
chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.detail: D1 hard rule C4 requires every feature's claim line to carry at least one inline citation; the sidecar preserves this invariant via the `citations` field, but downstream sibling lenses (D1 / D3 / D4) and any chapter synthesis must propagate the same invariant.

hard_rules_preserved: C4 (every claim line has a citation) — preserved by the `citations` field on every claim
F4 (every concept either has an Adopt? verdict) — preserved by `miniork_status` on every claim
F1 (breadth-defensible baseline) — preserved; this sidecar lists 40 features across 7 surveyed systems per D1's coverage map
F5/Q2 (no invented requirements beyond the D1 report) — every claim's `proposed_shape` is the D1-prescribed analog
